question.text: Which author wrote 'The Nightingale'?

results.hint: The same Danish storyteller wrote “The Little Mermaid” and “The Ugly Duckling.”
results.explanation: Hans Christian Andersen's fairy tale contrasts a living nightingale's song with that of a jeweled mechanical bird.

question.text: Aspirin was originally obtained from the bark of which tree?

results.hint: Its bark contains salicin, a natural compound that inspired the development of this pain reliever.
results.explanation: Willow bark contains salicin, which the body can convert into salicylic acid, a substance used in developing aspirin.

question.text: Which author wrote 'Trigger Warning: Short Fictions and Disturbances'?

results.hint: The same British fantasy writer created Coraline and the comic series The Sandman.
results.explanation: Neil Gaiman also wrote Coraline, which was adapted into an animated film.

question.text: Which sea creature strikes its prey with a club-like appendage at the speed of a bullet?

results.hint: Its spring-loaded punch can crack the hard shells of prey.
results.explanation: Mantis shrimp deliver blows with specialized forelimbs; some species instead use pointed limbs to spear prey.

question.text: Which band was co-founded by 'Pete Townshend'?

results.hint: Its rock opera Tommy includes the song “Pinball Wizard.”
results.explanation: The Who's Pete Townshend wrote much of Tommy, the band's 1969 rock opera.

question.text: In which year was Ben-Hur first released in the cinema?

results.hint: Charlton Heston starred in this biblical epic, which won 11 Academy Awards.
results.explanation: Ben-Hur became the first film to win 11 Academy Awards, including Best Picture.

question.text: Which author wrote 'Au soleil'?

results.hint: The author also wrote the short story “The Necklace.”
results.explanation: Guy de Maupassant’s Au soleil is travel writing based on his journey through Algeria.

question.text: What Chinese dynasty was overthrown in 1912?

results.hint: Its final emperor, Puyi, later became the subject of the film The Last Emperor.
results.explanation: The Qing dynasty's last emperor, Puyi, was only six when he abdicated in 1912.

question.text: Which composer wrote the song 'There's No Business Like Show Business'?

results.hint: The Russian-born American songwriter behind “White Christmas” also wrote this musical-theater standard.
results.explanation: Irving Berlin wrote the song for the Broadway musical Annie Get Your Gun, where Ethel Merman performed it.

question.text: Which author wrote 'Leatherstocking Tales'?

results.hint: His frontier novels include The Last of the Mohicans and feature the woodsman Natty Bumppo.
results.explanation: James Fenimore Cooper's five-novel cycle follows frontiersman Natty Bumppo; The Last of the Mohicans is its best-known installment.

question.text: Which author wrote 'Bouvard et Pécuchet'?

results.hint: The French novelist who created Emma Bovary also wrote this satire of two would-be intellectuals.
results.explanation: Gustave Flaubert's satirical novel remained unfinished when he died and was published posthumously.

question.text: What song did Michael Sembello have a hit with in 1983?

results.hint: It appeared on the soundtrack to the 1983 film Flashdance.
results.explanation: Maniac appears in Flashdance during a dance-training sequence; the climactic audition is set to Flashdance... What a Feeling.

question.text: Which of these countries borders Mali?

results.hint: Its former capital, Abidjan, is a major port on the Gulf of Guinea.
results.explanation: Ivory Coast also shares borders with Liberia and Ghana; its political capital is Yamoussoukro.

question.text: Which fruit comes in Tokay and Emperor varieties?

results.hint: They grow in bunches on vines, and some varieties are used to make wine.
results.explanation: Grapes include many named cultivars; Emperor is a large red variety commonly eaten fresh.

question.text: Which author wrote 'Im Schatten des Grossherrn'?

results.hint: The same German novelist created Winnetou and Old Shatterhand.
results.explanation: Karl May is best known for adventure stories featuring Winnetou, an Apache chief, and Old Shatterhand, a German traveler in the American West.

question.text: Which author wrote 'The Constant Gardener'?

results.hint: The same British novelist created the recurring intelligence agent George Smiley.
results.explanation: John le Carré, born David Cornwell, is best known for his espionage novels, many of which feature George Smiley.

question.text: What bay splits Virginia's part of the Delmarva Peninsula from the mainland?

results.hint: Virginia's Eastern Shore connects to the mainland by a famous bridge-tunnel crossing this waterway.
results.explanation: Chesapeake Bay is the largest estuary in the United States, fed by rivers including the Susquehanna.

question.text: Electrum is a natural alloy of gold and what other metal?

results.hint: Its partner is a precious metal whose compounds were once widely used in photographic film.
results.explanation: Silver gives electrum a paler color than pure gold, and naturally occurring electrum can vary in composition.

question.text: What art movement was Maurice de Vlaminck part of, known for its bold use of color?
Which director directed Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince?

results.hint: He also directed the final two films in the series.
results.explanation: David Yates went on to direct all four remaining Harry Potter films, more than any other director in the series.

question.text: Who succeeded Anthony Eden as the Prime Minister of the United Kingdom in 1957?

results.hint: As prime minister, he later spoke of a “wind of change” sweeping through Africa.
results.explanation: Macmillan remained prime minister until 1963, when Alec Douglas-Home succeeded him.

question.text: Which duo recorded the 1970 song 'El Condor Pasa (If I Could)'?

results.hint: Their folk-rock harmonies also appear on The Graduate soundtrack.
results.explanation: Simon & Garfunkel’s version popularized a Peruvian melody, with English lyrics by Paul Simon.

question.text: In which book does 'Alonso Quijano' appear?

results.hint: He is the aging Spanish gentleman who reinvents himself as a knight-errant.
results.explanation: In Miguel de Cervantes's novel, Alonso Quijano adopts the name Don Quixote and sets out on adventures as a knight-errant.

question.text: Which Formula One driver signed for McLaren in 1995 but was too big to fit in the car, missing the first two races?

results.hint: The 1992 world champion's stocky build caused the cockpit-fit problem.
results.explanation: Nigel Mansell had won the drivers' championship with Williams before joining McLaren; his 1995 return to Formula One was brief.

question.text: In Egyptian mythology, who was Horus' mother?

results.hint: She was the wife of Osiris and a major goddess associated with magic and protection.
results.explanation: Isis was also Osiris's sister; after he was killed by Set, she protected their son as he grew up.

question.text: Which musician wrote the song 'Knockin' on Heaven's Door'?

results.hint: The songwriter also wrote “Blowin’ in the Wind” and “Like a Rolling Stone.”
results.explanation: Bob Dylan’s song first appeared in the film Pat Garrett and Billy the Kid, in which Dylan also had a small acting role.

question.text: Which American alternative metal band released the studio album 'The Open Door'?

results.hint: Their breakthrough album Fallen featured the hit song “Bring Me to Life.”
results.explanation: Evanescence’s second studio album includes the single “Call Me When You’re Sober.”

question.text: From which part of the world does eggplant originate?

results.hint: Baingan bharta is a famous dish from the region where this vegetable originated.
results.explanation: Eggplant is native to India and nearby parts of South Asia, and it later spread to other regions through trade.

question.text: Which author wrote 'Jurassic Park'?

results.hint: The same novelist wrote The Andromeda Strain and created the television drama ER.
results.explanation: Michael Crichton trained as a physician, and many of his novels explore the dangers and consequences of scientific advances.

question.text: Which author wrote 'Neuromancer'?

results.hint: The author helped popularize the term “cyberspace” in an earlier short story.
results.explanation: William Gibson's novel won the Hugo, Nebula, and Philip K. Dick awards, making it the first novel to win all three.
